brazil_sources.title: PCDT Estratégias para Atenuar a Progressão da Doença Renal Crônica
key_findings: The Portaria explicitly states that the PCDT is national and must be used by state, DF and municipal SUS managers.
The PCDT recommends CKD-EPI and its displayed equation is adapted from Levey et al. 2009.
The PCDT CKD staging and urinary ACR categories are adapted from KDIGO 2012.

brazil_sources.title: Ministério da Saúde Linha de Cuidado — Doença Renal Crônica: Lesão Renal Aguda
key_findings: Ministry line of care explicitly applies KDIGO 2012 for acute kidney injury.

required_actions: Maintain CKD-EPI 2021 race-free as the default clinical calculation unless authoritative current guidance changes.
Keep the national SUS PCDT visibly separated from international KDIGO classification.
Do not execute the printed PCDT equation until its verified source conflicts are authoritatively resolved.
Never infer race or ancestry.
Recheck PCDT, SBN/SBPC-ML and Ministry AKI sources during final v2.0 qualification.
items.scope_pt: Há divergência entre o PCDT nacional vigente e a referência internacional mais recente usada pelo aplicativo; ambas devem ser explicitadas.
items.scope_en: The current national SUS PCDT differs from the newer international reference used by the app; both must be exposed explicitly.

items.feature: Hemodynamics — MAP / pulse pressure / Shock Index / Modified Shock Index

brazil_sources.title: Linha de Cuidados para Doença Trofoblástica Gestacional
key_findings: Uses maternal Shock Index and states values above 0.9 trigger the obstetric haemorrhage protocol.

brazil_sources.title: ANS methodological manual — sepsis line of care
key_findings: Uses MAP around the 65 mmHg threshold in septic-shock management.

required_actions: Preserve generic MAP, pulse pressure, SI and MSI mathematics.
Preserve generic threshold_classification_applied=false.
Keep MAP 65 mmHg restricted to explicitly selected septic-shock context.
Keep Shock Index >0.9 restricted to explicitly selected obstetric-haemorrhage context.
Do not infer a clinical context automatically.
Do not invent universal Brazilian MSI or pulse-pressure thresholds.
Recheck federal/national guidance during final v2.0 qualification.
items.scope_pt: Existem limiares brasileiros dependentes do contexto clínico, mas não um ponto de corte universal para os índices.
items.scope_en: Brazilian guidance contains context-dependent thresholds, not universal cutoffs for these indices.
bh3b_core_completed: Generic MAP, pulse pressure, SI and MSI mathematics preserved.
Explicit septic-shock context added for MAP >=65 mmHg.
Explicit obstetric-haemorrhage context added for Ministry Shock Index >0.9.
Context selection does not alter base calculations.
No MSI or pulse-pressure threshold added.
remediation_completed: Generic MAP, pulse pressure, Shock Index and Modified Shock Index calculations remain unchanged.
Generic threshold_classification_applied remains false.
Septic-shock MAP >=65 mmHg guidance is available only after explicit septic-shock context selection.
Ministry obstetric Shock Index >0.9 guidance is available only after explicit obstetric-haemorrhage context selection.
Shock Index exactly 0.9 does not satisfy the Ministry strict >0.9 contextual trigger.
No clinical context is inferred automatically.
No universal Brazilian MAP, SI, MSI or pulse-pressure classification has been introduced.
PT-BR, EN-GB, API, browser and offline behavior are integrated.

brazil_sources.title: Guia de Vigilância Integrada da COVID-19, Influenza e Outros Vírus Respiratórios
key_findings: Current Brazilian respiratory guidance uses SpO2 and clinical severity criteria for respiratory infection surveillance.
The audited national sources did not identify a general Brazilian replacement formula for P/F or S/F ratios.

required_actions: Keep P/F and S/F mathematics unchanged.
Record the Brazilian applicability audit in tool metadata.
Do not claim that the 2023 Global ARDS definition has been formally adopted by SUS without an explicit national source.
Retain the current rule against automatically diagnosing or staging ARDS from the ratios.
Repeat the Ministry/CONITEC/SBPT/AMIB source check during final v2 release qualification.
items.scope_pt: Nenhuma variante nacional geral de cálculo P/F ou S/F foi identificada no corpus oficial auditado.
items.scope_en: No general national Brazilian P/F or S/F calculation variant was identified in the audited official corpus.

items.international_reference: General acid-base, anion-gap, osmolality and hyperglycaemia references

brazil_sources.title: Fluxograma: Manejo da intoxicação por metanol pelo consumo de bebidas alcoólicas adulteradas
key_findings: The Ministry methanol pathway uses a toxicology-specific anion-gap formula including potassium.
It specifies a protocol-specific calculated osmolality and osmolar gap.
It uses methanol-specific acid-base thresholds and warns that normal early gaps do not exclude poisoning.

required_actions: Do not alter the existing general anion-gap or osmolality formulas.
Add a clearly separated Brazil Ministry methanol/toxic-alcohol context or mode.
Never apply the methanol formula automatically to general metabolic assessment.
Require measured osmolality when calculating an osmolar gap.
Preserve explicit source/version provenance for the Ministry toxicology pathway.
items.scope_pt: O Ministério possui fórmulas específicas para intoxicação por metanol; são contexto toxicológico e não substituem as fórmulas metabólicas gerais.
items.scope_en: The Ministry specifies formulas for methanol poisoning; these are toxicology-specific and do not replace the general metabolic formulas.

required_actions: No current remediation required; retain WHO numerical and Brazilian SISVAN layers separately.
